summary: The Tank 500 Hi4-T is the plug-in version of GWM's Prado-sized ladder-frame 4WD and it sells as a single Ultra grade alongside the new 3.0-litre diesel Lux and Vanta and a Vanta hybrid that the diesel is replacing. Australian reviewers agree it is the most genuinely off-road-capable plug-in hybrid on sale here - dual-range mechanical 4WD, three locking differentials, 3000kg braked towing and 6kW vehicle-to-load - and agree just as consistently that the 37.11kWh pack costs it the third row, dropping a seven-seat nameplate to five seats and 640L of boot. Scores land mid-field (CarsGuide 7.0, EV Central 3.5) and the recurring complaint is that the real numbers do not follow the claims: 10.0-10.2L/100km once the battery is flat against a 2.1L/100km label, and a measured 36-37kWh/100km in EV mode that delivers about 100km against GWM Australia's 120km NEDC claim and the 110km WLTC figure.
pros: The only plug-in hybrid in Australia with real off-road hardware: a dual-range transfer case with centre diff lock plus front and rear electronic lockers, 800mm wading depth and 213mm clearance, where the plug-in seven-seaters it is cross-shopped against - Mazda CX-80, Kia Sorento PHEV - are on-road crossovers with no low range at all

3000kg braked towing at full GVM (GCM is 6430kg against a 3430kg GVM, so the tow rating does not cannibalise the load rating) plus 6kW vehicle-to-load off the traction battery, which runs a caravan and a campsite from the same car

A 37.11kWh nickel-manganese-cobalt pack good for 110km of electric-only range on the WLTC cycle (GWM Australia quotes 120km NEDC) and 50kW DC fast charging on CCS2 (30-80 per cent in 24 minutes) - most plug-in hybrids at any price cannot DC charge at all, and the Mazda CX-80 and Kia Sorento carry 17.8kWh and 13.8kWh packs
7-year/unlimited-km warranty with no dealer-servicing condition attached, backed by 8-year/unlimited-km cover on the drive battery, 7 years roadside assistance and 7 years of capped-price servicing
300kW/750Nm and a claimed 6.9sec 0-100km/h for roughly the money of a mid-spec Toyota Prado or Ford Everest, both of which are four-cylinder diesels well under half the power
cons: The third row is deleted to fit the battery, and GWM's own spec sheet proves it: the hybrid grades are 7 seats with 795L behind the second row and 98L behind the third, while the Ultra Plug-In Hybrid is 5 seats with 640L and a blank cell where the third-row figure should be - so the seven-seat Tank 500 badge does not buy you a seven-seater

The 2.1L/100km combined label is meaningless once the battery is flat: GWM's own low-charge figure is 8.4L/100km, CarsGuide measured 10.2L/100km and Chasing Cars about 10.0L/100km, so a buyer who cannot charge at home is running a 2.8-tonne petrol 4WD on 91 octane

GWM Australia still quotes electric range on the superseded NEDC cycle (120km); the WLTC figure is 110km, and the measured 36-37kWh/100km EV consumption returned by Chasing Cars and EV Central implies about 100km from the 37.11kWh pack - CarExpert also found real-world range around 100km

At 2820kg kerb the plug-in carries 215kg more than the hybrid and its payload falls from 790kg to 610kg, so a 3000kg caravan's typical 300kg ball weight consumes half of what is left; reviewers also single out body roll, an adaptive cruise system that brakes far too early and sign recognition that misread school-zone limits

GWM's $79,990 drive-away price (VIC private; $78,990 for ABN holders) is the launch sticker, but it has been discounted almost continuously - $77,990 early-bird at launch, a $4,000 end-of-financial-year cut in June 2026, $76,990 on the road per EV Central, and $1,000 off to 30 November 2026 - while the Tank 500's five-star ANCAP result was awarded to the 2024 hybrid, with GWM saying at the plug-in's launch that it was still working with ANCAP on whether the heavier PHEV is covered
